skill.name: emergency-card
skill.description: Creates emergency medical information cards from local health records for travel, appointments, and urgent care. It highlights allergies, medications, conditions, implants, and contacts.
skill.summary: Builds printable and scannable emergency medical cards from recorded health data.
skill.author: huifer

security_audit.summary: Most static external-command findings are false positives from fenced Markdown and JavaScript examples. One bash example that runs a local Python generator is confirmed as an external command risk. No prompt injection was found, and one medium semantic finding covers sensitive health data export risk.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation before running scripts/generate_emergency_card.py, and document the expected script source.
Default to local-only output, mask contact details, and warn before generating QR codes or shareable files.
Provide offline HTML assets and discourage short-link QR codes unless a trusted private server is configured.

content.value_statement: Emergency responders need concise medical facts when a person cannot explain their history. This skill turns recorded allergies, medications, conditions, implants, and contacts into printable or scannable cards.
actual_capabilities: Extracts key facts from profile, allergy, medication, radiation, surgery, and discharge summary records.
Prioritizes life-critical allergies, active medications, urgent conditions, implants, and emergency contacts.
Produces HTML, JSON, text, QR code, and PDF-oriented output formats.
Supports adult, child, elderly, severe-allergy, A4, wallet card, and large-print variants.
Adds disclaimers and timestamps so users know the card is informational.
limitations: It depends on existing local health records and does not verify medical accuracy.
It is not a diagnostic, triage, or treatment recommendation tool.
QR codes and shared files may expose sensitive health data.
Referenced generation scripts are not included in the skill folder.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Travel
use_cases.description: Create a concise card with allergies, medications, implants, and contacts before a trip.

use_cases.title: Support Family Care
use_cases.description: Build a large-print card for an older adult, caregiver, or family emergency plan.

use_cases.title: Organize Clinic Intake
use_cases.description: Summarize recorded health facts for a doctor visit, intake form, or urgent care handoff.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Card
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a printable emergency summary.
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate an emergency medical information card from my available health records. Use a clear printable format and include only recorded facts.

prompt_templates.title: Make a Travel Card
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate request for a wallet card before travel.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a wallet-size emergency card for travel. Emphasize severe allergies, current medications, implants, and emergency contacts.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Caregiver Versions
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for multiple formats and privacy masking.
prompt_templates.prompt: Prepare both a large-print caregiver version and a compact QR version. Mask phone numbers except for the last four digits.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Missing Fields
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for source review before card generation.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my health record sources, identify missing emergency fields, then generate an A4 card and a text backup with update reminders.

output_examples.input: I need a travel emergency card for next week.
output_examples.output: A printable card with blood type, severe allergies, active medications, implants, contacts, disclaimer, and generation date.

output_examples.input: Create a card for my elderly father.
output_examples.output: A large-print emergency card with conditions, medications, contacts, and notes for first responders.

output_examples.input: Make a QR version for my phone.
output_examples.output: A QR-focused card summary that stores essential emergency details for scanning.

best_practices: Review the card with a clinician when possible before relying on it.
Regenerate the card after medication, allergy, contact, or implant changes.
Store printed and digital copies, but limit sharing to trusted people.
anti_patterns: Do not add diagnoses, medication advice, or treatment steps that are not in source records.
Do not publish QR codes or card files in public locations.
Do not use the card as a replacement for emergency services or clinician judgment.

faq.question: Can this skill give medical advice?
faq.answer: No. It organizes recorded facts and includes a disclaimer. It does not diagnose, triage, or recommend treatment.

faq.question: What records does it use?
faq.answer: It uses local profile, allergy, medication, radiation, surgery, and discharge summary records when available.

faq.question: Can it create printable output?
faq.answer: Yes. It supports HTML, text, JSON, QR, and PDF-oriented formats for printing, scanning, or archiving.

faq.question: Does it work offline?
faq.answer: Text, JSON, QR, and printed cards can work offline. CDN-based HTML assets may need initial network access.

faq.question: How often should I update the card?
faq.answer: Update it every three months, before travel, or after any medication, allergy, implant, or contact change.

faq.question: Is sensitive data protected?
faq.answer: It supports masking and local files, but users must control sharing, QR codes, and storage locations.
